artifacts.summary: Pins the exact per-site allowlist locations (git-commit-scoped.sh:499, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:1670, and git-commit-phase.sh's currently-absent Site 2 allowlist); reconstructs the real end-to-end path for task #467's historical drop (the task-creation commit, matched by exact timestamp and by the V10-specific zero-phase/zero-dispatch-seq issue shape); recommends one canonical shared library (engine_written_state_paths, modelled on lib/derived-artifact-probe-lib.sh) listing specs/TODO.md, specs/state.json, specs/events.jsonl, specs/errors.json; and maps the required git-staging-scope.md and test-fixture updates.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core, the proven pattern for a value multiple scripts must consult identically is a small sourced lib file (e.g. scripts/lib/derived-artifact-probe-lib.sh) exporting a function that echoes a compact JSON array, sourced defensively (`source ... 2>/dev/null`) by every consumer rather than each consumer hand-copying the same literal. Reuse this shape for any future 'same allowlist needed at N sites' defect instead of re-copying literals.

When reconstructing which of several near-identical code sites fired a historical issue-record.sh entry, the entry's own --phase/--dispatch-seq presence/absence (each call site passes a different, fixed subset of those flags) plus its exact timestamp matched against `git log` commit times is a reliable discriminator -- more reliable than inferring from which call site's pathspec 'could' have contained the path, since agent-composed bash (from a commands/*.md or SKILL.md prose template) is not guaranteed to match the template's literal example verbatim.
